ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz dominates Frances Tiafoe in opener to extend winning streak to 10 matches
Is this the week Carlos Alcaraz gets his hands on the Nitto ATP Finals trophy? He dispatches Frances Tiafoe with Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli to come in round-robin play; You can watch the ATP Finals in Turin this week on Sky Sports Tennis
Monday 16 November 2026 17:30, UK
Carlos Alcaraz powered past Frances Tiafoe 6-2 6-2 in just over an hour at the ATP Finals on Monday to stretch his winning run to 10 matches.
The Spaniard is aiming for his third straight title after lifting trophies in Vienna and Paris.
He's also aiming to claim the title at the season-ending tournament for the first time after losing last year's championship match in Turin to Jannik Sinner .
Sinner, the two-time defending champion at the ATP Finals, ended his season early due to a right knee injury.

Tiafoe's baseline game was no match for Alcaraz's power and movement, with the world No 3 dominant from the start.
Alcaraz has won three titles since returning to the tour at the US Open after a break of nearly five months due to a wrist injury.
The 2025 finalist quickly charged into a 4-0 lead as the American world No 8 was left looking helpless against Alcaraz's versatile play.
In a near-flawless first set, the Spaniard won 93 per cent of points on his first serve and a perfect 100 per cent on his second.
Before Tiafoe, making his ATP Finals debut, had time to react he was down a set and a break after half an hour.
He did earn three break points at 3-2 but could not make them count with Alcaraz holding and breaking again after a superb rally and down-the-line winner to make it 5-2. He served out the set in the next game.
"I would say this is the best I have felt so far in my career at this part of the season," Alcaraz said.
"I have never experienced something like this, this year. It was unusual for me, having a lot of months off the competition at home. So coming here I have a lot of energy and ambition and I am hungry for more."
"I tried to push him and let him know it is going to be a really great battle if he wants to win," Alcaraz added. "I am just really happy to start the tournament like this and hopefully I can keep it going."
Alcaraz vs Tiafoe: Tale of the Tape
Tim Henman, speaking on Sky Sports: "Alcaraz showed why he is the best and most exciting player in the world right now. Tiafoe will have to go away, lick his wounds and try to respond at this next opportunity.
"Just another incredible performance to marvel at. All aspects of Alcaraz's game firing on all cylinders."
On taking a step back in his schedule, Jamie Murray said: "Alcaraz has been quite vocal about the schedule and how he might miss more time on the tour to be fresher for the bigger tournaments.
"He is right because the calendar is so congested. The move to 12-day Masters events means players are away more, it's more mentally demanding - maybe more so than physical and he feels like he doesn't have to play every week of the year.
"He's going to decide what the biggest tournaments are for him and then he's going to try and peak for them."
Italy's Flavio Cobolli faces Daniil Medvedev in the other group match on Monday evening at the season-ending tournament.
